##  · K5b-od6-sweep — OD6: sweep of a quarantined device's handles vs map_device/dma_alloc NotPermitted

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 6

*Resolved in an earlier workspace; reopen it if the code has changed since.*

Decision references: docs/ANSWERS.md: answer 173, K5b plan OD6 (owner-approved), docs/KERNEL-SPEC.md: R10, Device

Evidence: Architect ruling applied: quarantine destroys the device object through R10 (KERNEL-SPEC R10, Device; answer 173 note) in 472a7b08f; the kernel's destroy_quarantined_devices and dma-reset-quarantine (BadHandle after quarantine) evidence it. Merged at b21cf53c8.

### Implementer 2 · Question

Event: `b5b1a728cee44fddd6022e351cae538d` · 2026-09-25T22:44:54Z

> K5b kernel commit, OD6. The approved plan says both (a) every handle to a quarantined device is swept, including handles in unreceived messages, and (b) map_device and dma_alloc on it return NotPermitted. §6's dma-reset-quarantine case asserts (b) after D2's death. With (a) done fully, no handle survives, so (b) can't be reached and the case would see BadHandle. The model (reference) does only (b): it flags the device and sweeps nothing.
> 
> My proposal: in the kernel, sweep handle tables with sweep_handles, and make is_live_device false for a quarantined slot, so message.rs is_live drops copies in unreceived messages at delivery. That is R10's existing path. Keep the NotPermitted checks in map_device and dma_alloc as a fail-closed guard. The quarantine case then asserts that its handle is gone: map_device and dma_alloc on its old index return BadHandle. It also asserts that a handle sent to it in a message before the quarantine arrives dropped. The model stays flag-only and returns NotPermitted, because it has no in-message liveness path; I'd note the difference in VALIDATION.md.
> 
> The alternative is flag-only in the kernel too, like the model: no sweep and NotPermitted everywhere. That is simpler, and the case stays as written, but it departs from OD6's "every handle swept".
> 
> I'm going ahead with the proposal, and I'll adjust if you rule otherwise.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `11d7dc003a688c4f3c82980c49662953` · 2026-09-25T22:45:59Z

> Ruling (Architect): sweep. OD6's owner-approved "every handle is swept, including handles in unreceived messages" governs, and so does answer 173's "not handed out again until reboot". The line in the §6 case that expects NotPermitted after the quarantine contradicts that. It is a slip in the plan and is not a separate rule. Device objects come only from the loader at boot (KERNEL-SPEC, Device), so once the sweep runs, no path gets a new handle to that MMIO base. No owner decision is needed.
> 
> One change to your mechanism: don't give is_live_device a quarantine special case. Destroy the MMIO device object with R10's existing message.rs::destroy_device: it calls sweep_handles and then free_device. The existing is_live_device check (the frame is no longer a device, or its id doesn't match) then drops the copies in messages that haven't been received yet, which arrive as 0 (R10). "Live" keeps its one meaning, and there's no new predicate. The plan already expects this: the registry flag is keyed by MMIO base and "outlives the device object". Before you rely on it, check two things: (1) nothing in D2's later teardown (dma_mapped, run slots, MMIO unmapping) dereferences the DeviceRef; they must key on the registry slot or base. (2) dma_release has the ss it needs to call destroy_device. If either check fails, fall back to your predicate and tell me why.
> 
> The NotPermitted guards in map_device and dma_alloc can't be reached through a handle any more. Don't add an ABI error that can't happen: KERNEL-SPEC's map_device error row stays BadHandle, WrongObject, OutOfMemory. If you want the guard, write it as assert!(!quarantined(base)), "I-DMA: a live device object names a quarantined device". That fails closed and loudly (tenet 2). Legacy MapMemory of a flagged base is still refused by base (§2), and that path stays reachable.
> 
> Case: after D2 is killed, map_device and dma_alloc on the old index return BadHandle, and a handle to the device sent before the quarantine arrives as 0. Keep the budget_usage and exhaustive-search checks as they are. P1-1 still holds because S comes from the runs and dma_mapped, not from handles.
> 
> Model: if it has per-process handle tables, sweep them too, so the kernel and the model both give BadHandle. Without in-message handles, record only that gap in VALIDATION.md. If it has no handle tables, stay flag-only with NotPermitted and record the difference. K5bQuarantinedDeviceUsable still applies either way.
> 
> Spec: when the docs commit lands, I'll write this into KERNEL-SPEC R10 and Device, and into answer 173's residual. The rule text: a device that fails its reset has its object destroyed as R10 does, and its base stays flagged until reboot. Tell me when that commit is ready. Proceed.

> Applied, in .worktrees/k5b. These are unstaged edits to two files only; I didn't commit, because your tests/ edits are live in that tree. Please stage and commit them by path: git add docs/KERNEL-SPEC.md docs/ANSWERS.md.
> - KERNEL-SPEC R10: a new closing sentence. A DMA device that fails the reset of a process's end (R11) is destroyed the same way, at that end: every handle naming it closes, in every table and every unreceived message, and its page goes back to its owner. Its base stays flagged until reboot, and a live co-holder keeps the mapping it already has (question 144).
> - KERNEL-SPEC Device: "None is created later, so a DMA device destroyed for failing its reset (R10) is gone until reboot."
> - ANSWERS 173 note: "two readings" is now "three readings". The third: "not handed out again" means the device object is destroyed as R10 does it; no handle can reach it, so there's no NotPermitted from map_device or dma_alloc. Provenance: Architect ruling, Wash QA K5b-od6-sweep, 2026-09-25.
> Your ecd34e43b fits: the R11 text, the call rows, the unchanged map_device error row and the IO-ARCHITECTURE "Reset before reuse" all agree with it. The kernel's destroy_quarantined_devices, which runs R10's destroy_device after terminate_process and kill_process, matches. From my side the spec for this thread is complete.
